title: Implicit Fine-tuning via Context Engineering: A Curriculum Learning Framework for Multimodal Entity Alignment

problem.claim: MMEA aims to identify equivalent entities across different modalities.

gap.claim: Existing black-box context-engineering methods rely on LLM parameter capacity and lack theoretical interpretability.

contributions.claim: The work theoretically validates mathematical equivalence between context engineering and model fine-tuning for MMEA, with prompt components simulating contrastive-learning-based sequential fine-tuning.
PTFEA is a curriculum-learning-inspired framework that translates fine-tuning strategies into interpretable context engineering.
PTFEA uses adaptive difficulty modulation and three-stage progressive inference to mirror curriculum-learning weights, sample selection, and gradient descent.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on five public datasets reportedly show that PTFEA consistently outperforms strong baselines.
On ICWIKI, PTFEA reportedly narrows the H@1 gap between Qwen2.5-72B and 14B to 0.6%.
Compared with MM-ChatAlign on ICWIKI, PTFEA reportedly reduces Qwen2.5-72B runtime from 21 hours to 1 hour and token consumption from 2200–3000 to 200–400, exceeding 80% reduction.

narrative_sequence.summary: MMEA identifies equivalent entities across modalities.
Existing black-box context engineering has unresolved capacity dependence and theoretical interpretability limitations.
The work establishes a mathematical equivalence between context engineering and fine-tuning in MMEA.
PTFEA translates fine-tuning strategies into interpretable curriculum-inspired context engineering using adaptive difficulty modulation and progressive inference.
The authors report performance, runtime, and token-consumption improvements across public datasets and on ICWIKI.

source_observation.claim: The framework translates curriculum-learning and fine-tuning concepts into staged context engineering with confidence-based difficulty modulation.

interpretation.claim: Structuring context information progressively may make black-box prompting more interpretable and reduce unnecessary inference cost.

application.claim: For multimodal alignment systems, consider staged information injection and confidence-based selection of context examples.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported benefits generalize beyond the stated MMEA datasets, models, or task conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the theoretical assumptions or proof details supporting the claimed equivalences.
The abstract does not provide dataset characteristics, baseline configurations, statistical variation, or ablation results.
The abstract does not describe the scope or license of the released code.
